items.title: Contextual right-hand pane (AuxPane) with a thread side panel as its first kind
items.summary: Generalise the read-only "room pulse" rail in SpacePage into one AuxPane shell (standard header with title/actions/back/close, persisted width, resize handle, docked-vs-overlay by width, focus hand-off) and register "thread" as the first pane kind, bound to a ?thread= URL param. The thread_id deep links that the Activity feed already emits then open the panel instead of being ignored; later kinds are run/agent-session, approval details and members.
items.whyItMatters: Agent runs produce long threads, and today replies continue inline (up to 30 turns per post), so a human cannot follow or approve a run without losing the room. A thread panel is table stakes in Slack, Teams and Buzz, and the AuxPane is the single container that live runs, approvals and members will also need, so every later visibility feature stops being per-feature layout work.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (thread panel, pop-out window, Threads view) for the pattern; Grok Bot for the pane mechanics
others: Teams (reply in place from an inbox thread card via a tree-grid compose box)
Buzz (one shared right panel for threads, canvas, members and agent sessions)
Slack help text on the Threads view (DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: thread panel 3 of 5 (Slack, Teams, Buzz); contextual right pane 3 of 5 (Grok Bot, Teams, Slack); table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Message carries thread_root_id; the pane route ?thread=<id> renders root plus replies with its own composer and scroll state; follow state per user feeds a Threads list with per-thread unread; pop-out opens the same route in a new window. The shell is one <AuxPane kind title actions onBack onDismiss> with an open -> closing (inert + aria-hidden, ~300 ms linger) -> closed state machine, width persisted per user, a role=separator handle with aria-valuenow and arrow-key resize, focus moved to the first enabled control, and a width breakpoint that decides docked vs overlay.

There is no thread panel, no followed-threads view and no consumer of the ?thread_id= links Activity generates. A shared-read refusal on the transcript currently renders as an empty thread rather than a "you cannot read these turns" state.

items.approach: Frontend Plane only for the first slice. (1) Build AuxPane in features/spaces/components, lifting the separator and persisted-width logic from the Inbox/Chat canvas code, keeping the existing 720 px collapse. (2) Add kind "thread": read ?thread= in SpacePage, fetch with the existing getSpaceThreadTranscript path (Model Plane Session Core stays the transcript owner), render root plus replies and the existing composer in reply mode; show an explicit "you cannot read these turns" state for refusals instead of an empty list. (3) Follow/unread-per-thread and a Threads view need the participant/unread projection (S1.7) in Application Plane and later push realtime. Pop-out window = same route in a new tab.
dependencies: Model Plane Session Core thread transcript read via the gateway (exists)
S1.7 participant/unread projection in Application Plane (for follow state and per-thread unread)
Push realtime or the Application delivery/projection outbox (category 09) for live replies
Run console components for the later run/agent-session kind (R-t1-12-03)
items.risks: Partial transcripts under deny-by-default shared reads must be shown as such. Keep the room-definition rule that configuration does not live in the room (docs/space-defenition.md: a room that shows configuration becomes a Copilot side panel): the pane should host conversation, run and approval content only. Focus traps and layout thrash at medium widths.

items.title: Cross-room navigation destinations: Home ("needs you"), Agents and Activity in the Core sidebar
items.summary: Add a typed destinations registry to the Core sidebar so a person can leave a single room: a Home/"needs you" page (unread, awaiting-approval and working counts across all Spaces they belong to), an Agents directory across rooms, and a cross-room Activity view, each permission-checked like any other action. Name the Home destination so it is not confused with the existing support Inbox (Zammad tickets and email at features/inbox).
items.whyItMatters: Once a user belongs to several Spaces with several agents, "what needs me" must be answered across rooms; approvals need a place to land. Four of five references have a first-class home/inbox/activity destination and the Space vision (Teams plus Slack) is hard to navigate without it. It is also the frame the thread panel, finder and sidebar organisation hang on.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (Agents, Workflows and inbox as first-class sidebar destinations, one shared right panel); Teams for app-bar mechanics
others: Slack (Home, Activity, Later/Saved rail destinations)
QM (permission-checked destinations() list)
Teams (app bar with pin/unpin, See-all flyout and keyboard drag-and-drop with spoken narration)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: File-based routes per destination; a pinned header component holds search plus fixed feature entries, below it fixed conversation groups plus user sections; a narrow rail switches tenants. Teams models the app bar as {appId, pinned, order} with a keyboard drag state machine (pickup, move, place/cancel) announced through a live region. Build as a <Rail> of route entries from a typed destinations registry, checked for permission the way QM does.

items.title: Make agent work visible in the room: ambient activity strip with latch/threshold rules, then typed transcript rows with grouping
items.summary: Slice 1 (S): turn the status-only lines ("Verevon is working in X", per-post working row, pulse card) into an activity strip near the composer with a headline derived from the latest run step and click-through to the run in the AuxPane, using latch and minimum-display-threshold helpers in a pure, tested lib. Slice 2 (M): replace the flat post list with a Row discriminated union (message, system/event, approval, tool or step, delegation, day and unread dividers, group) and a grouping pass that folds consecutive machine rows of one run into a collapsible group, collapsing completed work behind a "worked for N" disclosure while the answer stays open.
items.whyItMatters: Agent work is opaque in the room today: status lines exist but no step headline, no click-through, no tool or step rows and no grouping. This is the baseline's top "agent visibility" gap and the precondition for showing tool calls, delegations and approvals without drowning humans in a multi-agent room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz for the strip interaction; Grok Bot for the latch/threshold rules and the row-kind contract; QM for collapsing completed work
others: Buzz (headline rotation about every 2.2 s, hover list of working agents, agent badge with managed-by owner, address prefix)
QM (prompts over 2 lines collapse, completed tool steps collapse into one disclosure, paged history that does not yank the reader)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: activity strip 2 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot; differentiator); typed rows 3 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot, QM; table-stakes for human+agent rooms)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per room: typingUsers (presence TTL) plus workingAgents (run state from the owner projection). A committed-ids latch admits an agent to the visible set when it commits to a turn (not while reading) and releases it only at run end; a phase label shows only after a minimum display threshold. Headline = derive(lastStep) from the run event stream, rotated on a timer, with non-owners getting a generic "working". Rows: Row = message | send-message | event | notice | approval | attachment | spend | synthetic(day, unread, group); agent rows carry {agentRef, ownerRef}; a grouping pass folds consecutive machine rows of the same run into a group row with count and expand.

Define the Row union and grouping pass in lib with tests, then refactor SpaceRoomTimeline to render rows. Audience filtering per entry (S1.7): step text and tool output only for viewers entitled to read the run; everyone else gets the generic "working" and a group count.
dependencies: Run step events available at room scope through the gateway (Model Plane run stream)
AuxPane shell (R-t1-12-01) for click-through
Per-entry audience filtering / owner-private vs room-public output (S1.7)

Flicker if the latch rules are skipped once realtime lands. Row types multiply render cost until the timeline is virtualised (R-t1-12-06).

items.title: Personal sidebar organisation: stars, sections, per-group sort, hide, drag-and-drop, plus computed system sections
items.summary: Give each user a synced sidebar preference document (stars, custom sections, per-group sort, hidden refs) edited with drag-and-drop and a batch-selection mode, and add computed system sections over the same conversation summaries (Agent runs, Waiting for approval, Unread, Muted) that can be toggled without deleting anything. Ship layout changes behind a feature flag with a switch-back that only flips the preference.
items.whyItMatters: With agents creating many threads, a flat list degrades quickly. Per-user organisation keeps humans oriented without changing anyone else's view or any ACL, and "Agent runs" and "Waiting for approval" sections keep agent-generated conversations out of the human list without hiding them, which matters more here than in Teams.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (sort per group, synced sections and stars, dnd-kit sorting, More-unread pill); Teams for computed system sections and switch-back
others: Grok Bot (hide from sidebar, batch move/hide/delete for agents)
Slack (Priority sort, VIP break-through)
QM
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: organisation 4 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot, QM, Slack; table-stakes); system sections and view modes 1 of 5 (Teams; unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Per-user blob {stars:[ref], sections:[{id,name,refs[]}], sort:{group -> alpha|recent|priority}, hidden:[ref]} stored server-side and synced; groups render in fixed order, then user sections; sortable lists with a keyboard sensor; an IntersectionObserver on unread rows outside the viewport drives a "More unread" pill; selection mode with shift-range and bulk actions. Teams: system folders RECENT/MUTED/MEETING_CHATS as computed views toggled in settings, and a switch-back modal that preserves custom sections.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/core/components/sidebar/CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:104-232 and 281-321 (org room pinned first, thread pinned/unread/working dots, filter box)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/space-unread.ts (unread mirrors Application Plane read markers, but only for the open room)
verevonToday.gap: No user stars, custom sections, sort modes, drag-and-drop, hide or bulk actions, no filters or system sections, and unread dots exist only for the room open in this browser.

items.approach: Application Plane owns a per-user preference document (refs only, no room names, so retention and ZDR are not touched) read and written through typed gateway actions. Frontend Plane renders groups and computed sections from the conversation summaries, with the drag-and-drop and selection mode. Priority sort waits on the salience model already used by the Activity grammar. Note: package.json has no drag-and-drop or virtualisation library and runs Solid 2.0 RC, so check compatibility of solid-dnd or build keyboard-first sorting on existing primitives.
dependencies: Cross-room destinations and unread aggregate (R-t1-12-02)
Run and approval state present in conversation summaries (for system sections)
items.risks: Low authority risk, since preferences are per user and touch no Space ACL. Solid 2 RC library compatibility. Too many default sections clutters the list.

items.title: Composer for real work: attachments, slash commands, paste chips and ref-based "discuss with an agent" context
items.summary: Extend SpaceRoomComposer with attachments (including folder drop), a slash-command menu fed by the typed action registry and room skills, long-paste chips with a view/edit dialog, and saved model presets (QM allows up to 8). Add a selection mode to the Work, Knowledge and Activity lists so a human can select items and hand them to an agent as visible context chips that carry references, not copied content. Scheduled send and clips are later slices.
items.whyItMatters: Attachments and slash commands are what make a room usable for real work, and paste chips keep long pasted context legible for both humans and agents. Passing refs instead of text gives the human precise control over what the agent receives while owner planes re-check ACL and ZDR at use time, which fits the authority model and is a Buzz-only differentiator.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM for a human+agent composer; Slack for the human messaging set; Buzz for selection-to-context
others: Slack (formatting toolbar, clips, send-later)
Buzz (selectable list groups, count menu, discuss action, capped context block builder opening an agent chat or channel)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: composer 2 of 5 (Slack, QM; common, likely under-counted since attachments are industry-standard, INF); selection-to-context 1 of 5 (Buzz; unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Composer state {text, attachments[], chips[], loadout}; a paste handler turns text over N characters into a chip atom labelled from its first line; loadout presets upserted with cap 8; a slash token parser opens a command menu from a registry; scheduled send writes a job owned by the message plane. Buzz: buildContext(selection) produces a quoted, capped block of object refs and the action opens an agent chat or new channel with the block pre-attached as visible chips.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:597-772 (two-row textarea, model picker, skill chips, reply banner, ZDR refusals surfaced)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceWorkPanel.tsx:106-192 and components/SpaceKnowledgePanel.tsx:82-243 (read-only lists, no selection)
verevonToday.gap: No attachments, formatting, emoji, slash commands, clips, scheduled send, presets or paste chips, and no multi-select or "ask an agent about these" action. Every send is an AI invocation.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: composer state with chips that hold refs (documentId, runRef, threadRef) resolved by Data/Model planes at use time; attachments go through Data Plane documents with Space-bound ACL (never widened) and respect ZDR; slash menu reads human-eligible entries from shared/actions/action-registry.ts. Each append still needs a Control thread:append decision bound to the final bytes. Scheduled send needs an owner (Model Plane session or an Application Plane scheduler) and is deferred. Selection mode lands on the three read-only lists once chips exist.
dependencies: Human-only message path (category 01)
Attachments in Data Plane (category 08)
Room skills (S3.5) for slash completion
items.risks: Copying content into prompts would bypass owner ACL and ZDR, so pass refs. Content-bound append decisions complicate drafts and scheduled send. ZDR content must not reach external preview or embedding services. Attachments are table stakes in practice (INF): promote to priority if the category 01 human-only path lands first.

items.title: Virtualised room timeline with scroll anchoring, jump-to-latest and history paging
items.summary: Window the SpaceRoomTimeline rows, add a pure, unit-tested anchoring policy (keep the anchor offset on prepend, auto-scroll on append only while pinned to the bottom, show "Jump to latest" otherwise) and page older turns on demand instead of loading the whole thread on every poll. Keep aria-setsize/posinset so screen-reader order and find-in-page survive.
items.whyItMatters: Needed before push realtime and streamed agent output, otherwise the room jumps under the reader and long agent threads get slow. Not visible at today's low volume, but cheaper to build before the typed-row model hardens.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (written, tested anchoring policy on a patched virtual list, mobile IME handling)
others: Grok Bot (FLIP animation for rows shifting under late content, epoch-keyed layout cache)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Virtual list with measured row heights; anchoring state {pinnedToBottom, anchorRowId, anchorOffset}: on prepend preserve anchor offset, on append scroll only if pinned, show Jump-to-latest when not pinned and new rows arrive; ResizeObserver plus FLIP animates siblings when a row grows, disabled under reduced motion.

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/package.json (no virtualisation library; solid-js ^2.0.0-rc.0)
verevonToday.gap: No virtualisation, no scroll anchoring and no paging: the full thread list loads on every 6 s poll, so the view will jump once realtime or streaming lands.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: a windowing layer for the timeline with a standalone anchoring-policy module and lifecycle tests, plus a turn-paged history call from Model Plane through the gateway. Because the app is on Solid 2.0 RC with no virtual-list dependency, first confirm that @tanstack/solid-virtual works on Solid 2, otherwise implement windowing with IntersectionObserver and measured heights.

Turn-based history paging API in Model Plane
Push realtime (category 09) is the consumer that makes this necessary
items.risks: Virtualisation breaks find-in-page and screen-reader reading order unless handled; Solid 2 RC compatibility of third-party list libraries; unmeasured rows cause scroll jumps.

items.title: Universal finder: Cmd/Ctrl+K quick switcher over rooms, threads, agents and people, then the unified "To:" new-conversation picker
items.summary: Rebuild the Cmd/Ctrl+K overlay as a command palette with fuzzy match over rooms, threads, agents, people and human-eligible action-registry entries, with unread jumping and a hold-Cmd/Ctrl hint overlay; keep web search as a palette mode. Once DMs and a people directory exist, add a recipient-token "To:" field that finds or creates agents, people and groups, replacing the separate "+ New room", Create-agent and Bind-agent entry points.
items.whyItMatters: A switcher is a cheap daily-productivity win, and a palette over the typed action registry lets humans trigger agent actions under the same guardrails as buttons. The "To:" field collapses three creation flows into one entry point, which suits the Teams-plus-agents hybrid vision.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack for the keyboard model (switcher, unread navigation, All-unreads, F6 section cycling); Grok Bot for hold-to-reveal hints and the "To:" picker
others: Teams and Buzz almost certainly ship quick switchers (INF; no records)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: switcher 2 of 5 in records (Slack, Grok Bot; common, under-counted); "To:" picker 1 of 5 (Grok Bot; unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A global keydown router with scope (app, room, composer) and conflict rules; a palette component with fuzzy match over a combined directory; unread navigation iterates the cross-room unread list; hold-to-reveal arms a ~500 ms timer on modifier keydown, cancelled by other modifiers, keyup or blur, then shows numeric badges bound to Ctrl+1..9. Picker: a recipient token input over agents, team agents and people, free text offers "Create <name> agent", more than one recipient creates a group conversation.

Phase 2 (M): the "To:" picker over the Control roster (people) and Application agent bindings; creation still runs the two-step Application -> Control lifecycle and renders as pending, with born-narrow agent policy unchanged.

items.title: Agent computer view in the room: thumbnail preview that expands to an interactive modal with a control indicator
items.summary: Show an agent's browser or computer as a glanceable preview card in the room (periodic frame or low-rate stream) that expands to an interactive modal with a screen switcher, a "control: agent | you" badge and an idle pause. Build it in the Frontend Plane as a UI over Quarry-executed browser sessions, hosted in the AuxPane for the run, and gated on read entitlement for the run.
items.whyItMatters: Core to the vision that agents work like a human with their own PC and browser: members see what the agent is doing in the room they share, and human takeover for secrets or CAPTCHAs has a natural home. Only Grok Bot has the glanceable-to-interactive progression, which makes it a high-leverage differentiator.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (preview card to interactive modal, multi-screen, control owner badge)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Computer view modes {preview, interactive}: preview is a periodic frame or low-rate VNC stream in a card; the modal is interactive VNC with a screen switcher and a control-owner badge (agent or you); an idle pause with wake and retry; a REC overlay while recording.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:497 (browser with human takeover, dashboard only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/agents/components/AgentRunConsole.tsx:551-569 (run screenshots, run console only)
verevonToday.gap: Nothing is reachable from a Space and there is no per-agent computer; the takeover browser and run screenshots are reusable building blocks only.

items.approach: Frontend Plane card plus modal in the AuxPane. Model proposes browser actions, Quarry executes or rejects them under BrowserBroker grants; the preview streams frames Quarry exposes, and takeover requires a human grant. Show only to members entitled to read the run, never share credentials across members, and do not retain frames beyond policy.
dependencies: Per-agent browser or sandbox capability (agents category)
Quarry frame streaming
AuxPane shell (R-t1-12-01)
items.risks: Frames may contain sensitive or ZDR data, so respect privacy tier and read entitlement and never copy frames to retention paths; takeover must not widen what the room can do.

items.title: Room header and pulse rail: live counts, pinned posts first, user-added tabs and a budget meter
items.summary: Keep the six fixed cockpit tabs as the default but add header counts (open approvals, running work, documents) from existing projections, show pinned posts first, and allow user-pinnable extra tabs (link, document, later canvas) stored as Space metadata. Add a usage meter with warning thresholds to the pulse rail once per-Space cost attribution exists.
items.whyItMatters: Lets people see what an agent can use and what it is doing before invoking it, matching the Teams tabs-on-a-channel habit and QM's "the room's computer" view. Since every post is a paid model turn, shared rooms also need visible budgets before the limit is hit instead of only a refusal after.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (scope-centred page and top-bar tool buttons with 60 s cached counts); Slack for user-added tabs and bookmarks; Grok Bot for the usage meter
others: Slack (Pins tab auto-created on first pin, bookmark folders)

items.title: Space UI quality baseline: localised activity grammar, shared announcer, reduced-motion and density, and failure screens
items.summary: Four independent small tasks. (1) Move the activity grammar labels and the forced nb-NO date formatting onto the i18n catalog and the viewer locale, with an optional friendlier phrasing layer. (2) Promote the page-local chat live region into a shared announcer (tick-keyed so repeats are read), add agent state to row aria-labels and a navigate-with-focus helper. (3) Audit Space animations for prefers-reduced-motion and add a density token. (4) Add a root error boundary with an honest failure screen, a static cannot-connect page from the gateway, a redacted diagnostic export and start-up milestones to telemetry.
items.whyItMatters: English-speaking users currently see Norwegian activity labels on the product's strongest UX asset; Agent rooms change constantly, so without an announcer every live row is a noisy live region and enterprise buyers expect accessibility; and a blank page on a gateway or render failure contradicts the "never go dark" stance applied everywhere else in the Space. All are cheap now and costly to retrofit.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (friendly activity vocabulary, announcer and pane focus rules); Teams (row narration, start-up milestones); Slack (cannot-connect page with log download); Buzz (reduced-motion gate, 3-level density)
others: QM (agent-facing copy reviewed like UI)
Teams (device-memory efficiency mode)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: friendly copy 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, QM); accessibility 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, Teams); motion/density 2 of 5 (Buzz, Teams); shell failure UX 2 of 5 (Slack, Teams); differentiators
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Catalog map from activity kind to localised friendly label. Announcer: two hidden regions (role=status, role=alert) each wrapping a span keyed by a counter so identical messages repeat, with announce(text, politeness). Pane navigation: outgoing pane inert and aria-hidden until animationend, then focus to the landing target once headings exist, skipped if focus is already elsewhere. Density: a data attribute scaling spacing variables; motion components check prefers-reduced-motion. Failure UX: milestone events (loaderStarted, firstPaint) to telemetry, critical load failure routes to an error page listing network checks and a "download logs" bundle.

items.title: Long-tail Space UX, build on demand: multiview tiling, agent-led first-run welcome, What's New and admin notices, non-web link interstitial
items.summary: Four independent slices, none of which blocks the vision. (a) Multiview: tile several rooms or agent sessions with a dockview-style layout once AuxPane and run components are self-contained. (b) Welcome: seed the org room with an agent introduction and role/tools questions that feed the three agent templates. (c) What's New panel and admin-only notices for policy rollout. (d) Route non-http(s) links in agent-posted content through a confirmation with per-host memory.
items.whyItMatters: Multiview is a real edge for operators supervising several agents (QM only); a welcome post where an agent introduces itself removes the empty-room first impression; admin notices help owners learn which deny-by-default agent policies to enable; and a link gate reduces risk from model-generated links.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (multiview with tile limits and per-pane density); Grok Bot (onboarding flow and fail-open gate); Teams (feedback, What's New, admin campaigns); Slack (protocol interstitial with per-host allowlist)
others: Buzz (agent-led welcome channel)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: multiview 1 of 5 (QM); onboarding 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, Buzz); What's New 1 of 5 (Teams); link interstitial 1 of 5 (Slack); differentiator to unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Multiview: dockview-core layout with MAX_TILES = 16, per-pane drag payloads and a serialised layout synced per user. Onboarding: gate state machine checking -> probe -> landed | onboarding | shell with a saved seen flag that fails open for returning users. What's New: feed items with an index and campaigns targeted by role and flag. Interstitial: intercept non-http(s) schemes, show a modal, store an allowlist of {protocol, hostname} per user.

items.approach: Frontend Plane for all four. Multiview after AuxPane (R-t1-12-01), push realtime (a 6 s poll per tile multiplies polling cost) and self-contained room and run components. Welcome: seed a post and template agent proposals that a human confirms (agents may not create bindings themselves), with claims derived from observed facts, not timers. What's New from a static release feed, admin notices through Control role targeting. Link gate: extend the markdown link sanitiser so non-http(s) schemes never auto-open.

items.risks: Tile polling cost; agents must not self-create bindings; notice noise. Verify the link-rendering and feedback surfaces before scoping slices (c) and (d).

strengthsToKeep: Six-tab cockpit (Chat, Work, Knowledge, Activity, Agent, Members) exposes more of an agent's working context than Slack or Teams, with hash-tab deep links and legacy-hash handling: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceCockpit.tsx:61-110, 150-151.

Activity grammar (verb, object, outcome) is ordered by consequence and salience, mutates live rows in place and has lenses, equal to or ahead of Buzz and QM on "one event log, many lenses": apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/activity-grammar.ts and components/SpaceActivityFeed.tsx (keep it as the single vocabulary).

Honest-state UX is enforced in code: the unavailable[] contract, tabs that tell empty from could-not-load from not-published, an unobserved room treated as unknown rather than idle (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/space-live-work.ts), and unknown authors kept distinct from former members. One exception to fix: the swallowed transcript read failure at apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:201.

Destructive actions arm in place before they run (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceConfirmButton.tsx), and personal-Space deletion returns a receipt from each plane (apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/spaceDeletionReceipts.ts), more careful than the references.

Approvals are already a typed in-timeline row with a composer-visible refusal path for ZDR and budget limits: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceApprovalPanel.tsx and components/SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:541-567.

Durable per-room read markers with a browser mirror that defers to the owner plane (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/space-unread.ts, apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/spaceReadMarkers.ts) and a typed action registry (apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/actions/action-registry.ts) provide the authority-checked foundation for the palette and cross-room aggregates.
